caseStudy.name: Tsho Rolpa glacial lake, Rolwaling, Nepal

bookmarks.name: Tsho Rolpa lake

bookmarks.name: Rolwaling valley

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Radar backdrop (median HV)

explanation.what: The median HV radar brightness of all dates, used as a quiet background.
explanation.inspect: Use it to find your way around the valley.

limitations: A median of several dates, so it belongs to no single date.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Radar brightness (HH)
layers.unitsNote: Gamma-0 backscatter, linear in the file, shown in dB.

legend.highLabel: Bright: rough rock, slopes facing the radar

explanation.what: How much of the radar pulse bounced back to NISAR on each date. HH means sent and received horizontally.
explanation.measures: Backscatter strength. Calm water acts like a mirror and sends the pulse away, so the lake is dark.
explanation.inspect: Step through the dates and watch the dark lake shape. Click a point to read the stored value.
explanation.establishes: Where open water and rough surfaces are on each date. It does not show depth or water level.

limitations: Provisional data: calibrated and partly validated, not for final scientific conclusions.
Dates alternate between dual-pol 10 m and quad-pol 20 m acquisitions. All are shown on a shared 20 m grid.
Radar shadow behind steep slopes also looks dark. Shadows do not change between dates on this track, so they do not move.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Colour radar (HH, HV, HH/HV)

keys.label: Black: calm water, or radar shadow
Purple: smooth bare rock, ice, snow
Bright blobs: steep slopes facing the radar (distorted)

explanation.what: Two radar channels and their ratio mixed into one colour picture.
explanation.measures: Red is HH brightness, green is HV (which rises with rough, jumbled surfaces such as debris and vegetation), blue is HH divided by HV.
explanation.inspect: The lake is near black. Smooth rock, ice and snow look purple. Rough moraines and debris look yellow-green. Bright blobs are steep slopes squashed by the radar's side view.
explanation.establishes: A visual guide only. Colours are not measurements, so the inspector does not sample this layer.

limitations: Provisional data: calibrated and partly validated, not for final scientific conclusions.
Dates alternate between dual-pol 10 m and quad-pol 20 m acquisitions. All are shown on a shared 20 m grid.
Radar shadow behind steep slopes also looks dark. Shadows do not change between dates on this track, so they do not move.
Colours are stretched for display. Compare shapes between dates, not exact colours.

layers.name: Lake edge measured from radar
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NISAR GCOV (NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, ASF DAAC)
limitations: Drawn from radar at 20 m: edges are accurate to about one or two pixels (20 to 40 m).
All dates are drawn on top of each other. Where they overlap, the lake edge did not move.

layers.attribution: Scenario by CascadeLens from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and the NISAR lake area
layers.name: River route below the dam
limitations: Traced on a 60 m terrain model with depressions filled. It follows the valley floor, not the exact river channel.

layers.attribution: Scenario by CascadeLens from Copernicus DEM GLO-30 and the NISAR lake area
layers.name: Flooded area if a 20 m breach (scenario)
limitations: Scenario only: the widest case (highest peak flow, smoothest channel) for a 20 m breach, from 60 m terrain cross-sections every 500 m.
The peak is not reduced downstream, so the area is larger than a real flood of this size would cover far from the lake.

layers.attribution: Copernicus DEM GLO-30: © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
layers.name: Terrain shading (Copernicus DEM)

explanation.what: Shaded relief of the valleys below the lake.
explanation.measures: Nothing: light and shadow from the terrain heights.
explanation.inspect: Use it to follow the river route.

limitations: Shading only, from 60 m averaged heights.

layers.name: Can the radar see it? (surface change)
layers.attribution: Derived by CascadeLens from NISAR GUNW (NASA/ISRO) and Copernicus DEM GLO-30

keys.label: No valid data in the product

explanation.what: Could a surface change between these dates be seen here?
explanation.measures: Each spot gets its reasons kept separate: inside the frame or not, data present and unflagged by the product's own mask or not, hidden by terrain (layover or shadow, from the radar's own viewing angles and the elevation model), and signal quality. Missing inputs are marked Not assessed, never Usable.
explanation.inspect: Click any spot to see which reasons apply there. Grey and dark areas are not 'no change': they are places the radar could not judge.
explanation.establishes: Where a NISAR result can be trusted for this task. It does not say whether anything changed.

limitations: Only active layover and shadow from the local slope. Passive shadow cast by a distant ridge is not modelled, so some shadowed valleys may be marked visible.
The DEM is Copernicus GLO-30 resampled to the analysis grid; small features below the grid size are smoothed.
Coherence comes from the 80 m product, so features narrower than about 80 m are mixed with their surroundings.
Coherence also falls for reasons that are not surface change (wet snow, vegetation, a long time gap). The disturbance task only says whether a change could be seen, not whether one happened.
An exact zero in unwrapped phase is treated as unwrapping fill. A component's own reference pixel can be exactly zero, so at most one real pixel per component may be lost.
Products are Provisional.

layers.attribution: NASA/JPL-Caltech/ISRO, NISAR; distributed by ASF DAAC
layers.name: Ground stability (16–28 Aug)

explanation.what: How alike the radar echoes were on 2026-08-16 and 2026-08-28, from 0 (nothing alike) to 1 (identical).
explanation.measures: Interferometric coherence. Bare rock and the moraine dam stay bright. Water, moving ice and fresh snow go dark.
explanation.inspect: Compare the dam at the lake's western end with the ground around it.
explanation.establishes: Where the surface stayed the same for 12 days. It does not say how far anything moved.

limitations: Provisional data.
Steep slopes facing away from the radar are dark because of radar shadow, not change.
Twelve days in the monsoon: wet snow and rain lower coherence even on stable ground.
Coherence shows where the surface stayed the same. It is not a measurement of movement.

lake.name: Tsho Rolpa
lake.basin: Rolwaling Khola, then Tamakoshi and Sun Koshi, in the Koshi Basin
lake.published: Published figures: about 1.55 km² (2008 survey), 1.61 km² (Peppa et al., 2020, satellite images) and 1.65 km² (2022 DHM bathymetric survey, as reported by Dialogue Earth).

terrain.attribution: Copernicus DEM GLO-30: © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA
terrain.note: Heights from Copernicus DEM (2011 to 2015 survey), not from NISAR. The radar is draped on top.

lake.method: Dark area in HH + HV below -7 dB after 3x3 smoothing on a 20 m grid. The range reruns it at -6 and -8 dB.

disturbance.label: Usable
disturbance.meaning: The radar saw this ground clearly before and across the event, so a change here would show.

disturbance.label: Seen, but not reliable
disturbance.meaning: The ground was already incoherent in the baseline pair, so a drop across the event cannot be told apart from normal noise.

disturbance.label: Hidden by terrain
disturbance.meaning: Layover or radar shadow: the slope's geometry hides it from this viewing angle.

disturbance.label: No valid data in the product
disturbance.meaning: Inside the frame, but the product holds no value here, or its own mask flags it (water, an invalid subswath or an image anomaly).

disturbance.label: Outside the frame checked
disturbance.meaning: Outside the radar frame assessed here. A neighbouring frame or another track may cover it, but it is not checked yet: no conclusion, not no change.

disturbance.label: Not assessed
disturbance.meaning: An input needed for this check is missing or invalid here (terrain geometry, or the baseline pair). No conclusion.

movement.label: Usable
movement.meaning: Phase is coherent and reliably unwrapped, so ground movement could be measured here. Nothing has been measured yet.

movement.label: Seen, but not reliable
movement.meaning: Phase is too noisy (low coherence) or was not reliably unwrapped here, so no movement value can be trusted.

movement.label: Hidden by terrain
movement.meaning: Layover or radar shadow: the slope's geometry hides it from this viewing angle.

movement.label: No valid data in the product
movement.meaning: Inside the frame, but the product holds no value here, or its own mask flags it (water, an invalid subswath or an image anomaly).

movement.label: Outside the frame checked
movement.meaning: Outside the radar frame assessed here. A neighbouring frame or another track may cover it, but it is not checked yet: no conclusion, not no movement.

movement.label: Not assessed
movement.meaning: The terrain geometry needed for this check is missing or invalid here. No conclusion.

coherenceMin.provenance: Project choice. 0.3 is a common lower bound for usable L-band phase; results at 0.2 and 0.4 are reported alongside so the choice can be checked.

layover.value: range slope toward the radar > incidence angle
layover.provenance: Standard SAR geometry (layover occurs when the terrain slope facing the sensor exceeds the incidence angle).

shadow.value: range slope away from the radar > 90 deg - incidence angle

coherenceProduct.value: unwrappedInterferogram coherenceMagnitude, 80 m, sampled nearest onto the 40 m grid
coherenceProduct.provenance: The coherence that belongs to the unwrapped phase and shares its mask; the same layer the app shows.

sensitivity.denominator: All analysis cells inside the frame footprint, over the whole case area.
sensitivity.rule: The same rule as the movement class, with only the coherence threshold changed.

limitations: Only active layover and shadow from the local slope. Passive shadow cast by a distant ridge is not modelled, so some shadowed valleys may be marked visible.
The DEM is Copernicus GLO-30 resampled to the analysis grid; small features below the grid size are smoothed.
Coherence comes from the 80 m product, so features narrower than about 80 m are mixed with their surroundings.
Coherence also falls for reasons that are not surface change (wet snow, vegetation, a long time gap). The disturbance task only says whether a change could be seen, not whether one happened.
An exact zero in unwrapped phase is treated as unwrapping fill. A component's own reference pixel can be exactly zero, so at most one real pixel per component may be lost.
Products are Provisional.
